research_question: What existing formal/security mechanisms already cover semantic preservation, proof-carrying history, single-use state/authority, supply-chain provenance, attestation, runtime action governance, and current SQLite recovery risk, and therefore collide with or constrain LSCW-001?
queries: proof carrying code policy machine-checkable proof
proof carrying data all history comply property
translation validation compiler run refinement simulation
linear types aliased resources capability state properties
RATS attestation evidence verifier relying party freshness
proof carrying agent actions runtime governance 2026
runtime proof of execution governed agent actions 2026

primary_sources.title: Proof-carrying code
primary_sources.collision: A producer attaching a machine-checkable proof of policy compliance to untrusted code is established prior art. LSCW cannot claim proof-carrying safety as novel.

primary_sources.title: Proof-Carrying Data and Hearsay Arguments from Signature Cards
primary_sources.collision: Proofs attached to data/messages can attest that the data and all of its history comply with a specified property. This is a strong collision for history-carrying semantic witnesses.

primary_sources.title: Translation validation
primary_sources.authors: Amir Pnueli, Michael Siegel, Eli Singerman
primary_sources.collision: Validating each concrete translation run against a refinement relation in a common semantic framework is established. LSCW's stage-local semantic conservation must be viewed as a generalized lifecycle application, not a new compiler-verification principle.

primary_sources.title: The CompCert verified compiler
primary_sources.collision: Whole-compiler semantic preservation by compositional simulations is established and demonstrates that representation changes need not imply semantic changes.

primary_sources.title: Typestate: A Programming Language Concept for Enhancing Software Reliability
primary_sources.collision: Restricting legal operations according to current state is established. LSCW's transition-state legality is not novel by itself.

primary_sources.title: Linear types for aliased resources
primary_sources.collision: Linear types can track aliasing and state-dependent properties. Single-use witness semantics has strong prior art and must earn value from lifecycle composition, not linearity alone.

primary_sources.title: Formal Mechanised Semantics of CHERI C: Capabilities, Provenance, and Undefined Behaviour
primary_sources.collision: Unforgeable capabilities and provenance have rigorous semantics. LSCW cannot claim provenance-bound capabilities as a new primitive family.

primary_sources.title: in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes
primary_sources.collision: End-to-end software supply-chain step integrity and verification are established. Build-to-deploy provenance should reuse rather than reinvent in-toto/SLSA concepts.

primary_sources.title: SLSA Provenance specification
primary_sources.collision: Verifiable where/when/how build provenance is current industry specification. Trusted-builder/artifact identity should align to SLSA/in-toto where practical.

primary_sources.title: in-toto Attestation Framework Specification
primary_sources.collision: Authenticated metadata is explicitly bound to immutable subjects and predicates; LSCW should not invent a competing generic build-attestation envelope.

primary_sources.title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
primary_sources.collision: Evidence, verifier appraisal, attestation results, relying-party policy, and freshness are established roles. LSCW should distinguish evidence from authority and keep owner policy external.

primary_sources.title: Proof-Carrying Agent Actions: Model-Agnostic Runtime Governance for Heterogeneous Agent Systems
primary_sources.collision: Portable action certificates with pre-admissibility, open, assumptions, approval, and outcome closure strongly collide with any claim that action-level proof-carrying governance is novel.

primary_sources.title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
primary_sources.collision: Canonical action identity, approval binding, receipt integrity and runtime-portable projection are very close prior art for the action/effect segment of LSCW.

primary_sources.title: Proof of Execution: Runtime Verification for Governed AI Agent Actions
primary_sources.collision: Contract + causal event stream + replay context and validator-checkable invariants collide with execution/replay attestation. LSCW's claim must remain lifecycle semantic conservation, not generic proof-of-execution.

primary_sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging - WAL-reset bug
primary_sources.collision: The accepted target's storage risk is real and version/topology dependent; current docs say the bug is fixed in 3.51.3 and later. This supports binding actual consumed runtime identity rather than inferring safety from package/source labels.

primary_sources.title: SQLite Release 3.53.4
primary_sources.collision: 3.53.4 includes the WAL-reset fix and is the exact current V4 private-runtime target in PR359.

destruction_result: No component idea survives as world-new. Proof-carrying compliance, history-carrying proofs, translation validation, typestate, linear capabilities, artifact attestation, action certificates, execution proofs and provenance are all established. LSCW can survive only as a Frank-specific lifecycle composition candidate: one common typed semantic-dimension basis, explicit stage transform budgets/residuals, dual semantic/product identity, and consume/reissue lineage spanning compile->installed start->actual consumed runtime->effect->reentry->recovery.
